author: Phan Nguyễn Mai Phương
purpose: course-alignment evidence for report and slides

model_specs.hgb169: historical hgb_baseline169 outer predictions; 126 rolling + cycle + 42 history features

endpoint_definition.cycle_origin: floor(fraction*lifetime), clamped to first persisted cycle
endpoint_definition.aggregation: equal-engine MAE; pooled row RMSE; total and equal-engine NASA retained

model_selection_status: No new selection; evidence compares persisted models and keeps the historical calibrated169 reference separate.

recommendation.decision: Use HGB169 as the main predictor candidate for the report because it is better on the common full-trajectory and endpoint panels, subject to the stated conditional-bootstrap and historical-inspection limits.
recommendation.whole_process_warning_readout: Do not claim an unconditional whole-process improvement: under the fixed threshold30 policy HGB169 is less timely, while under threshold40 it is slightly more timely with a small burden increase.
recommendation.warning_policy: Keep the historically calibrated169 policy as a separate reference and report fixed-policy sensitivity. A deployment policy must be declared and validated separately from selecting the predictor.
recommendation.test_reporting: Keep test reporting separate; these outputs do not use test labels to choose the predictor or warning policy.

fixed_warning_policy_status: thresholds 30 and 40, persistence 1, lead requirement 30; common sensitivity policies, not newly calibrated

calibrated169_reference.historical_procedure: hgb_baseline169 with inner-selected warning policy per outer fold
calibrated169_reference.condition: historical nested-policy readout; not comparable to the fixed-policy sensitivity table as a calibrated-vs-fixed claim
calibrated169_reference.scope_limit: outer predictions and inner selection were historically inspected; no new refit or independent blind confirmation

smoothing.causal_definition: mean of cycles max(1, t-29)..t; output interpreted only from cycle 30 onward
smoothing.purpose: descriptive evidence that smoothing attenuates short-term variation while retaining broad change
limitations: C-MAPSS has no clean sensor ground truth, so reduction in first differences is a proxy for attenuation, not proof of noise removal.
Trailing means create boundary delay and are not a causal mechanism explanation.
No smoothing parameter was fitted, searched or selected from labels.
The analysis does not establish that smoothing improves RUL prediction.
No new model fitting or test-label read was performed.
Paired bootstrap is conditional on saved predictions and excludes refit, seed and selection uncertainty.
Historical inspection means this evidence is not an independent blind confirmation.
The 126-versus-169 comparison changes feature representation as well as feature count; it does not isolate architecture.
Causal smoothing descriptors do not identify true sensor noise and do not establish RUL benefit.
